unresolved_added: The source has a visible title and Introduction but no Summary or Abstract; the four-task and three-method ladders substitute for front-matter synthesis.
The official task statement is unavailable, so deliverables are reconstructed only from paper-internal goals.
HEV, PHEV, and BEV descriptions are class summaries rather than a representative global fleet sample.
The continuous Bass equation includes alpha_t while the discrete equation drops it without defining alpha_t or explaining the discretization.
Time-invariant m,p,q are assumed; market saturation, policy, prices, technology turnover, and regional heterogeneity are omitted.
The ACO procedure lacks colony size, parameter bounds, step rule, pheromone law, evaporation rate, convergence tolerance, random seed, and comparison with OLS/NLS/MLE.
Newton gradient descent is invoked inside an absolute-error objective without explaining nondifferentiability or the update equation.
Only p and q are reported even though C={m,p,q}; the fitted market potential m and fit residuals are absent.
A +/-5% local p,q perturbation is called acceptable from plotted error bars without a numerical criterion, global sensitivity, or held-out forecast.
Projected adoption is treated as proof of feasibility and economic attractiveness, which exceeds a sales forecast.
Oil-import and price projections are visually asserted without a displayed regression equation, coefficient table, uncertainty, or counterfactual controls.
EV indirect emissions use one 2009 USA average generation mix and average plant factors; marginal generation, losses, region, year, battery, and infrastructure are omitted.
Petroleum generation is ignored and renewable/nuclear emissions are treated as nearly zero, so the boundary is operational rather than lifecycle.
GM notation shifts among E, E0, and E1; Y uses E rather than explicitly E0, and the time-response expression visibly prints T(1).
The printed residual mean error has no absolute value or square, so positive and negative errors can cancel.
GM and BP-ANN weaknesses motivate combination, but no network architecture, training split, loss, hyperparameters, convergence, or benchmark comparison is supplied.
Large-scale use is defined as an 80% share without decision justification or threshold sensitivity.
The 81.9% 2020 EV share and emission forecasts are internal projections rather than observed validation.
The pollutant reduction paragraph switches from NOx to NO2 and converts CO2 with a shadow price whose arithmetic does not reconcile 3.704 billion tons with 37 billion dollars at 39.97 dollars/ton.
Healthcare values are cited as fixed dollars without population, exposure, time, price year, sign convention, or uncertainty; sulfur dioxide is negative under the current mix.
DEA requires comparable DMUs, yet the displayed data describe one EV package and the paper does not show CV input/output data used to obtain efficiency 0.7.
DEA inputs and outputs mix annual dollars per ten million EVs with unclear taxes/transfers and no price year or normalization.
Sensitivity ranges in Table 10 lack the perturbation program and units; interpreting the smallest range as causal policy leverage is unsupported.
Battery charging, second-life storage, recycling, and Si-O2 claims are qualitative and lack degradation, safety, material, cost, and lifecycle evidence.
The prediction that battery capacity will eliminate long-range limitations is asserted without a technology or infrastructure scenario.
Historical CV consumption is replaced by its average for the next decade based only on visual steadiness; no structural-break or uncertainty test is reported.
The fossil-fuel calculations combine 97%/67% shares and 14%/28% efficiencies without a transparent dimensional derivation or consistent transportation/grid boundary.
Calling a 2011 saving equal to 1.1% and a 2020 saving equal to 49% a fit to the actual scenario is not validation; both are model projections conditional on 2009 consumption.
The AHP judgment matrix is expert-supplied without elicitation evidence; RI=0.96 is questionable for n=4 and makes the near-threshold consistency conclusion fragile.

Impact prices xi_i are multiplied by generation-source shares alpha_i without defining why environment, society, business, and individual dimensions map one-to-one to thermal, hydro, nuclear, and wind.
The optimization omits alpha1+alpha2+alpha3+alpha4=1 and nonnegativity, so the source-share interpretation is not enforced.
Thermal and nuclear chained inequalities mix installed capacity, a maximum-load coefficient, and annual generation without a documented common time or energy unit.
Water and wind availability quantities are compared directly with electricity generation; conversion efficiencies, time indices, geography, and units are unresolved.
The balance includes BEV and PHEV but omits HEV electricity use, charging losses, temporal load, transmission, storage, and reserve margin.
Accepting an unspecified feasible solution whenever an optimum does not exist is a deliberate fallback but gives no quality, dominance, or solver-status guarantee.
Figure 11 is used both for the AHP structure and the 2020 USA generation chart; the text also calls the 2020 chart Figure 12, creating a source-number mismatch.
The assessment says ACO overcomes data dependence and the hybrid is more accurate without comparative error metrics, and admits the energy constraints were simplified deeply.
Conclusions and suggestions are substantially more certain than the evidence: no uncertainty propagation, held-out validation, causal design, or decision-stability analysis is supplied.
References on physical pages 19-20, headers, table cells, chart labels, formula-only blocks, URLs, and cited wording are excluded from positive language evidence.
